about.title: About
about.paragraph1: I'm a back-end-focused software engineer. At Itaú BBA I build cloud-native services on AWS (Lambda, ECS, API Gateway, DynamoDB), with asynchronous messaging on SQS and SNS, and integrate internal APIs with external services, handling credentials, secrets and access policies in a regulated environment.
about.paragraph2: Before that, at a legal-tech startup, I pulled the AI out of a monolithic CRM into its own microservice. As a freelancer, I built and maintain BRCO, which turns Brazil's national goat and sheep nutrition equations into a free web calculator. For my thesis, I architected a traceability platform with Solidity contracts on Polygon and a custodial wallet that hides all Web3 complexity from users.
about.research1: 3D computer vision for weight estimation (30th SIC)
about.paragraph3: My way of working is to find the bottleneck, propose the change and measure the result. That's how the AI's response time at Lexa dropped from up to 12 minutes to at most 3, on a lean team with the product in use.

highlights: Proposed and architected the AI module (lexa-ai) from scratch as an independent microservice, decoupling AI from the monolithic CRM.

highlights: Managed a portfolio of concurrent clients (doctors and clinics) from first contact to activating their AI agent in production on WhatsApp.
Reached the team's fastest activation time since I joined, in a process that used to take months.
Won the internal campaign to reactivate inactive clients, ahead of the whole team.
On my own initiative, created support materials that reduced onboarding friction and documented the team's processes from scratch; management adopted them and they're still in use.

brco.stack: Node.js, Express, Prisma, Django, Vue.js, Docker, AWS (EC2, Lightsail)
highlights: Took Brazil's national nutritional-requirement equations for goats and sheep (BR-CORTE) out of academia and shipped them as a free web calculator.
First version in Django with JWT, Pytest and PDF reports; rewritten in Node.js/Express with Prisma, CSV export and least-cost diet formulation via linear programming.

In 2026, hardened the platform: regression tests locking every equation's output (which caught a production 500), HMAC-token admin login replacing a key exposed in the front-end, and a persistent database with migrations on boot.

cases.title: Case studies
cases.subtitle: Four systems told end to end: the problem, the architecture and what worked.

brco.label: Freelance · in production
brco.title: BRCO: nutritional requirements calculator
brco.problem: Nutrition for goats and sheep in Brazil is usually formulated with foreign tables that don't reflect tropical animals or diets. Farmers, students and researchers had no free, Brazilian tool to calculate requirements and build a diet.
highlights: Three calculators built on Brazil's BR-CORTE equations: nutritional requirements, a feed's energy value (TDN) and least-cost diet formulation via linear programming, with a looser second attempt when the ideal model has no solution.
The equations live only in the back-end, behind Zod validation, rate limiting and helmet; the HTTPS front-end reaches the EC2 API through a Netlify proxy.
Regression tests lock every equation's output and caught a production 500; the admin panel moved to an HMAC token instead of a key exposed in the front-end.

organizador.label: Serverless on AWS · AI
organizador.title: Finance assistant on Telegram
organizador.problem: Logging expenses in an app is tedious enough that nobody keeps it up. The idea is to log them the way you'd say them ("spent 45.90 at the grocery store on my Nubank card") and let the system handle statements, installments and recurring items.
highlights: AI interprets, code executes: Gemini's output goes through a Pydantic contract before touching the database, and deletes or large amounts require a button confirmation.
FIFO queue grouped per user: one chat's messages are processed in order, Telegram retries are dropped and failures land in an alarmed DLQ.
CDK infrastructure deployed on every push via GitHub Actions and OIDC (no AWS keys in GitHub); database migrations run in a Lambda and CloudFormation rolls back if they fail.

tcc.label: Blockchain · Thesis
tcc.title: Animal traceability on blockchain
tcc.problem: Fraud in cattle vaccination and transport records is hard to prove, because the data lives in systems that can be altered.
highlights: Hybrid design: only each critical event's hash goes to Polygon (L2); full data stays in PostgreSQL.
Back-end custodial wallet: users never touch a private key or pay gas.
Database and chain kept consistent with atomic transactions, plus 95%+ test coverage on the contracts.

lexa.label: Microservices · AI
lexa.title: lexa-ai: AI as a microservice
lexa.problem: The AI ran inside a monolithic CRM and could take up to 12 minutes to answer a WhatsApp message.
highlights: AI isolated in its own reusable, horizontally scalable service.
Response time cut from up to 12 min to at most 3 (~75%).
Agents fed by a scraper of Brazilian court systems.

orbit.title: Orbit
orbit.description: Self-hosted dashboard for people running many projects and environments: service health, logs, secrets and GitHub in one place, so you find out something is down before your users do.
highlights: HTTP, TCP, PostgreSQL and Redis health checks, with Z-score anomaly alerts over latency history.
Live server logs over SSH, streamed via WebSocket and filterable by level.
Per-environment .env vault with AES-256-GCM and GitHub login showing branches, last commit and open PRs.

exlege.title: Exlege
exlege.description: AI-powered case-law research for lawyers: natural-language search, a chat that cites the decisions, and alerts when a new ruling on a topic comes out.
highlights: Daily automated collection of STJ decisions, classified by area and summarized in plain language by an LLM in a single JSON-output call.
Semantic search with embeddings in PostgreSQL + pgvector, filters by court, area and date, and ready-to-copy citations.
Personal data (CPF, CNPJ, phone) masked before storage, and blue/green deploys on AWS Lightsail with CI/CD.

Automatic migrations on startup and a Vue 3 + Pinia front-end organized with Atomic Design.
